newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Sept 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
President Suharto, speaking at the opening of an international conference on infrastructure, said that Indonesia needs $10 billion more in private investment to finance its own development.

Japan warned Indonesia again on Monday that it will take Jakarta to the World Trade Organization over the Timor national car policy. The comments were made by the Vice Minister for International Trade and Industry at a press conference in Tokyo.
President Suharto said that Indonesia is a democratic state and that the people hold the highest sovereignty.
Foreign investment approvals fell by 25.3 percent for the first eight months this year to $22.2 billion, from $29.7 billion in the same period of last year.
Head of the Indonesian Armed Forces (ABRI) General Feisal Tanjung said Monday that planned training exercises were not meant as a show of strength in the South China Sea.
